tasks.short: Prepare elementary course outlines and materials

steps.what: Read curriculum requirements and choose suitable course objectives for the actual students
inputs: existing pupil learning and access information

steps.what: Write the course outline and objective explanations from the teacher's selected requirements

loop.purpose: Organize supplied teacher notes into an outline tied to selected curriculum objectives.
loop.input: Teacher-selected objectives, source requirements and existing preparation notes.
loop.output: Draft outline with objective references and proposed explanatory wording.
loop.check: Teacher checks every objective mapping, factual claim, sequence and access assumption; the model does not choose pupil goals.
loop.stop: Unsupported mappings or inaccessible suggestions stop for manual rewrite after at most two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied explanatory wording needs text organization; reuse existing outlines and native fields wherever sufficient.

steps.what: Prepare the actual course material files with appropriate layout and teacher-chosen content
Check the complete objectives, outline and materials against requirements and actual accessibility needs
Prepare the actual printed and physical materials needed for the courses of study

tasks.design: Use existing curriculum references in {LMS}, draft outline wording from teacher-selected objectives, and reuse the actual material-file styles in {DOCS}. The teacher retains goal choice, substantive corrections, full access checks and physical classroom preparation {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlines require varied explanatory wording, while existing material files repeat layout operations.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting and native document styles address those separate operations without choosing learning outcomes.
tasks.still_hard: Sequence, developmental fit and access depend on the children and require teacher checking and real materials.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher chooses suitable goals and can reject content that is technically plausible but unusable in the classroom.

ambition.what: Prepare the same suitable course materials with less first-draft and layout work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound outline drafting and native document styles can reduce wording and layout operations while teacher selection and accessibility checks remain necessary.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual course preparation through classroom-ready materials, not a new preparation report or external release. The files are actually used in teaching.

The existing curriculum publisher supplies objective code, text, version and requirements; the current teacher/support team supplies existing access information. s1 counts reading, any manual extraction and objective choice. s2 retains current preparation-note capture and corrections, not a free clean requirements brief.

Test existing outlines, native styles and reusable materials first. s2 retains 17.5 of 35 units for note capture and rewrite; s3 retains 15 of 20 units for actual content/access layout and removes only 5 repeated style/header operations. s4 counts full independent source/meaning checking and s5 all physical preparation. {OTHER} means classroom printing and physical teaching aids.
Ordinary same-system working saves occur inside s2/s3 at near-zero fully retained time, without approval or benefit. No model makes pupil decisions or infers diagnoses, and no recording is assumed.

Additional source packaging, new dictation if needed and failed-draft/style repairs beyond retained case corrections are counted below. Estimates are unmeasured and do not inherit study percentages or prompt time shares. Pupil access and applicable national school consultation requirements need confirmation.
unknowns: Current reused outlines and style templates
Actual access adaptations and physical materials
research_questions: Trace one course's objective choices, outline wording and physical preparation.
Test a wrong objective mapping and an inaccessible layout, retaining manual repair.

already_counted.description: Objective selection, actual source/note capture, correction, substantive material layout, full checks and physical preparation remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Additional source packaging/dictation, curriculum/style upkeep and failed-draft repair beyond retained corrections.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=25+17.5+15+10+10=77.5. Gross 22.5 less 4 added work gives net 18.5. Conservative case: a new curriculum sequence requires 31 of 35 outline units and a nonstandard access format retains 18 of 20 material-file units. Six gross units less 4 upkeep gives 2; all goal choice, checks and physical preparation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the existing daily-living skill goal and current pupil support requirements
Prepare the actual hygiene, safety or food-preparation learning space and aids for instruction
Instruct students in daily living skills through actual demonstration, supported practice and responsive feedback

tasks.design: Use the existing {DOCS} skill-plan link for immediate reference reading. Keep the actual preparation and living-skill teaching with the teacher and physical learning aids {OTHER}; the change does not automate practical instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: The immediate skill plan and support references may require repeated opening.
tasks.enabler_now: A native reference link may remove that small navigation action.
tasks.still_hard: Safe supported practice and the appropriate level of assistance depend on the actual child and setting.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices what the child can do and provides appropriate support and feedback.

ambition.what: The same practical living-skill instruction remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing skill-plan links can reduce reference navigation but do not replace practical daily-living teaching.

assumptions: Boundary includes immediate plan reading, real physical setup and instruction. Course preparation and separately required pupil progress-record writing are separate tasks; no post-instruction report is invented here.

The existing teacher/support plan supplies skill goal, agreed support and material reference. s1 retains reading and missing-reference lookup; s2-s3 retain every physical and instructional action. {OTHER} means actual classroom daily-living practice aids, not sensors or an automated kitchen.
Test native links first. The change removes only 1 of 5 repeated navigation units, retaining 4 for reading; the full 95 preparation/instruction units remain. Shares are unmeasured design estimates.
No new structured pupil data, recording, diagnosis, scoring, send or formal commit is assumed. Link repair beyond case reading is additional upkeep, counted below.
research_questions: Observe plan reading, physical setup and direct instruction separately; confirm whether the link already exists.

already_counted.description: Actual skill-plan reading, physical setup and all instruction remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: Maintain and repair existing skill-plan links beyond normal lesson reading.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=4+20+75=99. Gross 1 less 0.5 upkeep gives net 0.5. Conservative case: an altered support plan requires 4.5 of 5 reading/navigation units; the remaining 0.5 gain just covers upkeep. Practical work is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the existing elementary program, actual evaluation evidence and curriculum constraints
Collaborate with teachers and administrators to evaluate the program and decide proposed developments or revisions
outputs: actual program evaluation and revision decisions

steps.what: Write the actual program revisions and their rationale in the working elementary program document
inputs: actual program evaluation and revision decisions

loop.purpose: Express the actual agreed revisions in the existing program structure without deciding program policy.
loop.input: Current program text, actual revision decisions and teacher's existing discussion notes.
loop.output: Draft revised sections with explicit changes and source decision references.
loop.check: Teacher checks every changed objective, responsibility and rationale against the actual discussion and curriculum; preserve unresolved questions.
loop.stop: An unsupported agreement or conflicting requirement stops for manual revision and further staff clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied program prose needs text organization; fixed fields and unchanged sections require no model.

tasks.design: Link the actual program evidence in {DOCS} and {LMS}, then draft the working revisions from the staff's actual decisions. Collaboration, evaluation and complete revision checks stay human; no school policy is adopted or published by the drafting helper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program evidence can require repeated retrieval, and agreed revisions need translating into consistent program prose.
tasks.enabler_now: Native references and bounded drafting can reduce those operations while preserving tracked changes.
tasks.still_hard: Program priorities, evidence quality, inclusion and agreement across staff require real deliberation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher contributes classroom experience and distinguishes actual agreement from an unresolved proposal.

ambition.what: The same program collaboration retains teachers' and administrators' decision rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source references and bounded drafting can organize actual program revisions without replacing staff evaluation or formal program adoption.

assumptions: Boundary is collaborative program evaluation/development and the actual working revisions used by that group. Formal school-wide adoption and publication are separate authority actions if present; the working document is not relabeled as such a commit.

The existing program owner supplies versioned objectives and requirements; existing evaluation producers supply dated evidence and source references. s1 counts actual reading, source retrieval and manual fallback, not a newly commissioned evaluation. s2 produces real deliberation and decisions; s3 retains current note capture, substantive revision and complete checks.

Test current document links, tracked changes and revision templates first. s1 removes 4 of 20 repeated navigation units. s3 retains 22.5 of 30 units for capture, content revision and full checks, removing repeated prose organization only. These are unmeasured estimates, not shared percentage cuts.

Ordinary same-system working saves stay within retained s3 time, ungated and with no gain. No new meeting report, staff recording or automatic program decision is introduced. Additional source packaging and failed-draft repair are counted below.
Other staff's actual participation remains unchanged and outside this teacher's denominator. Applicable access and national school consultation arrangements need confirmation.
unknowns: Actual program evidence and working revision process
Actual formal adoption and publication route
research_questions: Trace one real proposed revision from evidence and staff discussion into working program text.
Test unresolved disagreement without converting it into an agreed program change.

already_counted.description: Evidence reading, all staff deliberation, actual revision capture and complete content checks remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: Package actual decision sources, maintain references and repair failed drafts beyond retained revision checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=16+50+22.5=88.5. Gross 11.5 less 3 additional work gives net 8.5. Conservative case: archived evaluation evidence retains 19 of 20 lookup units and disputed program wording retains 27 of 30 revision units. Four gross units less 3 upkeep gives 1; staff deliberation is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer on lesson plans and schedules

steps.what: Read the approved curricula and existing lesson requirements before conferring with staff
Confer with staff members on lesson content, learning needs and feasible scheduling arrangements
Write the actual shared lesson plan from the staff's content and support agreements
Assemble the exact proposed lesson calendar entries from the agreed staff, rooms and times
Confirm the exact final lesson calendar entries under the participating teacher's actual scheduling responsibility
Publish the exact authorized lesson schedule entries to the shared staff calendar
Save the shared lesson plan in its existing working document

tasks.design: Reuse curriculum references and the existing shared lesson-plan fields in {DOCS}, then assemble proposed {CALENDAR} entries from actual staff agreements. Preserve staff deliberation and real confirmation of the exact final schedule before publishing; the ordinary lesson-document save remains ungated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed lesson details may be copied into a plan and then re-keyed into shared calendar entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native template fields and calendar drafts can reuse actual confirmed details and publish the authorized snapshot.
tasks.still_hard: Lesson suitability, staffing and room conflicts need real agreement rather than an inferred availability list.
tasks.human_edge: Teachers decide how the lesson will support actual pupils and whether its practical arrangements work.

ambition.what: The same collaborative lesson planning and scheduling retain staff decision rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native plan fields and calendar drafts can remove real repeated scheduling entry, while exact staff agreement and lesson-content decisions remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual staff conferring, the shared lesson plan and an actual shared-calendar publication. The calendar action is distinct from ordinary document persistence; no extra approval of the author's note is added.

The curriculum owner supplies approved objective reference/version; s1 retains reading and manual lookup. s2 produces actual lesson, support, staff, room, start/end time and calendar audience agreements through the existing conversation, counting any manual availability checking. s3 retains actual plan capture and checking. No free structured availability feed is assumed.

Test current plan fields and calendar drafts first. s1 removes 1 of 10 navigation units; s3 removes 5 of 25 units of repeated objective/staff/header entry and retains 20 for substantive plan writing/checks. s4/s6 count only real manual calendar drafting and shared publication actions, not already automatic runtime or a same-system save.

s5 is the actual participating teacher's existing final scheduling confirmation, not a new supervisor or self-approval. Confirm the real authority route before use; its time stays other-role work and is not a focal saving. The exact entries must exist before confirmation; changed staff, time, room or audience voids a1. This is a working-lesson schedule, not autonomous allocation.

s7 is ordinary author persistence at the minimum share, fully retained and ungated. The document is read for actual lesson delivery. Failed entry/publish repair and additional source packaging are counted below rather than silently sent to another teacher.
Shares are unmeasured workflow estimates. If the real calendar already creates/publishes the entries natively, those actions earn no new saving; do not invent manual re-entry.
unknowns: Actual shared-calendar use and manual entry
research_questions: Observe an actual staff-planning episode through the shared calendar, identifying real duplicate entry.
Test changed room/time after confirmation and failed calendar publication; require fresh authorization of changed entries.

already_counted.description: Reference reading, staff conversation, substantive plan capture/checking and ordinary persistence remain in s1, s2, s3 and s7.
Actual participating-teacher final scheduling confirmation remains other-role effort and is not deducted from focal savings.

incremental.description: Maintain plan/calendar fields, package changed agreements and repair failed calendar drafts/publications beyond retained planning checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact s5-confirmed lesson calendar entries, staff, rooms, dates/times and shared audience; any change voids authorization.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B=95, R=9+45+20+0+0+1=75. Gross 21.0526 less 3 upkeep gives net 18.0526; high rounded down to18. Other-role confirmation is excluded from B. Conservative case: unlinked curriculum retains all 10 reading units, bespoke lessons retain 24 of 25 plan units and incompatible calendar templates leave 8 of 10 draft units manual. Only 7 focal units are removed including the real 4-unit publication: 7/95*100 less3=4.3684, low rounded down to4.3.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher retains practical teaching, pupil needs and program decisions while reducing selected preparation wording, repeated fields and genuine calendar re-entry.
skills_to_grow: Check curriculum mappings and access adaptations
Separate actual staff agreements from inferred availability
Bind calendar publication to the final agreed entries
role.ambitious_version: Keep accessible lesson preparation and collaborative schedules traceable to actual teacher choices and staff agreements.
